transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-02
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Rahul Patel (Redwood SE), Nadia Gomez (Redwood Product), Maya Chen (CTO - Emberline), Liam O'Rourke (Head of ML), Priya Kapoor (Security), Aaron Mills (Platform).

[00:00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll kick off in a minute. I'm Sofia, AE on the Redwood side, with Rahul our SE who will walk through the console and some cost attribution flows.
[00:00:12] Maya: Hi all, Maya here. We're mostly looking to understand how we can map inference costs back to our feature teams and also what operational controls we'd need for a HIPAA-adjacent workflow.
[00:00:20] Rahul: Great, thanks Maya. Quick agenda: console tour (per-route dashboards), usage analytics (token level), Optimize suggestions, and then Q&A. We'll show an example project that approximates your multi-team setup.
[00:00:37] Liam: Quick note — we have a 2k token summarization route used heavily by our clinician notes feature; latency targets are 300-500ms p95, and cost per call needs to stay below $0.06.
[00:00:49] Rahul: Noted. We'll point to the route-level latency and cost panels for that exact scenario.

[00:01:15] Rahul: (screen share) Okay, here's the Console home. Top line shows cluster health and total spend last 30 days. Jumping into Routes.
[00:01:35] Aaron: Is that spend already broken down by model and route?
[00:01:40] Rahul: Yep — the routes view includes a table of routes with columns for model variant, average tokens in/out, p95 latency, calls per minute, and cost per call. You can also tag routes with business unit metadata, which is how you map back to your feature teams.
[00:01:55] Nadia: We also support exporting allocation tags to your billing export so your finance team can ingest route attribution.
[00:02:05] Priya: On the security side, how is the tagging data stored — is it embedded in application telemetry or in the control plane? We need to know for our audit scope.
[00:02:15] Rahul: Good question. Route metadata is stored in the control plane (customer-managed in Private), and route attributes are not logged in payload-level logs by default; we keep the mapping in the management layer and only include tags in the billing export. For Hosted we have strict retention defaults and you can opt into longer retention if you need it for cost reconciliation.
[00:02:35] Maya: That helps. Can you show the 2k token route's breakdown?

[00:02:50] Rahul: Pulling it up — here's 'clinician-notes-summarize'. You can see an overview graph of token volume by day, model version rollouts, and a waterfall cost breakdown. The waterfall shows raw model compute cost, batching savings (if enabled), cache hits, and network egress.
[00:03:12] Sofia: Note the 'Optimize' panel on the right — it surfaces suggested knobs: batch size, KV cache prefix enablement, and a quantization recommendation for compatible model families.
[00:03:24] Liam: For quantization — do you have an expected accuracy delta estimate? We can't have hallucinations increase.
[00:03:30] Rahul: The console shows a quality delta estimate based on our eval suite for common tasks; for summarization it suggests int8 with an expected BLEU/ROUGE delta of <0.5% for the current model family. We always recommend running a short eval on your prompt set first.
[00:03:44] Maya: Where do we upload that prompt eval?
[00:03:47] Rahul: There's an 'Evals' tab in the Optimize area — you can upload CSV prompt/expected output pairs and run quality vs cost curves. We'll share a template.

[00:04:10] [00:04:10] Priya: SSO and SAML — can we enforce role-based access to specific routes? For example, only the ML team can deploy model variants.
[00:04:18] Nadia: Yes — RBAC maps to SSO groups. We support SCIM, SAML 2.0, and IdP-initiated flows. Roles can be scoped to projects and routes. There are audit trails for changes with user, timestamp, and diff.
[00:04:32] Aaron: Is the audit log tamper-evident?
[00:04:34] Rahul: For Private deployments we integrate with your KMS and can ship signed logs to your SIEM; hosted customers can export logs and we provide an append-only export.

[00:05:05] Rahul: Back to cost — here's the per-token cost breakdown. You can toggle to show amortized GPU time per token, and the view correlates batch size and concurrency to effective cost per token. 
[00:05:18] Liam: That amortization line — is that empirical from our own runs or a modeled projection?
[00:05:22] Rahul: It's empirical when you run Redwood benchmarks against your model version; otherwise it's a projection based on the model profile. In Dedicated we can bind the measured kernel performance which makes that number tighter.

[00:05:45] Maya: How do we handle fallback when Dedicated is out of capacity — will things route to Hosted and change billing?
[00:05:52] Rahul: Great question. We support routing policies by priority: Dedicated -> HostedFallback. The Console shows the historical fallback volume and cost delta. You can set auto-fallback thresholds and also automatic model variant substitution to keep latency SLOs.
[00:06:10] Priya: From a compliance pov, if fallback routes to Hosted does that create data residency issues?
[00:06:16] Rahul: It could. We surface region-level routing policies and you can disallow cross-region fallback. For regulated workloads we usually recommend Private or Dedicated with strong routing locks.

[00:06:40] [00:06:40] Rahul: Now look at the 'Cost attribution' tab — you can group by route tag, model, or origination team. There is an export button; the exported CSV includes columns: route_id, tag_business_unit, date, calls, total_tokens_in, total_tokens_out, cost_compute, cost_network, cost_other.
[00:06:58] Aaron: Perfect, our finance team can ingest that. Does that output include UUIDs so we can join to our internal cost center table?
[00:07:04] Rahul: Yes, route_id is a stable UUID you can map in your CMDB.

[00:07:20] Sofia: Side note — we have a 'per-token attribution API' as well so you can programmatically fetch attribution for arbitrary time windows.
[00:07:28] Liam: That would be ideal for near-real-time dashboards we run internally.

[00:07:50] Priya: On data retention — what are the hosted defaults? We need logs for 1 year for audits.
[00:07:56] Nadia: Hosted default retention for control-plane metadata is 90 days; we offer extended retention add-ons for compliance up to multi-year. For payload logs we have strict redaction off by default — customers can opt into retention and provide a business justification.
[00:08:12] Priya: KMS integration — we use AWS KMS with BYOK; is that supported for Private?
[00:08:18] Rahul: Yes, Private supports BYOK/HSM integration. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys in select regions via a partner integration.

[00:08:45] [00:08:45] Liam: Can the Optimize suggestions be applied as experiments? We want to A/B batch/quantize and measure regression.
[00:08:53] Rahul: Absolutely — rollouts support canary and A/B. You can define rollout policies on a per-route basis, set traffic weights, and the Console will show a side-by-side metrics comparison including quality deltas if you attach evals.
[00:09:10] Maya: Show the canary UI?

[00:09:18] Rahul: (navigates) Here — create rollout -> source variant -> target variant -> traffic split. You can also set automatic rollback on quality degradation or latency breach.
[00:09:30] Aaron: How are quality degradations detected — do you need labeled data?
[00:09:33] Rahul: We use your eval sets for automatic checks; there is also a heuristic monitoring mode based on toxicity scores, repetition, and perplexity surges as fallbacks.

[00:09:52] [00:09:52] Maya: Let's talk numbers — if we moved the clinician-notes route to Dedicated with 4 GPUs, what would typical per-call cost look like vs Hosted?
[00:10:01] Rahul: Without exact benchmarks, a rough ballpark for your model family is Hosted: $0.08 per 2k call at current throughput; Dedicated (4x) could get that to $0.03-0.05 depending on batching and cache. We'll run the benchmark Rahul promised to give a tighter figure.
[00:10:18] Liam: That's promising. Can you also show how to tag cost to our feature teams retroactively for the last 90 days?
[00:10:26] Rahul: Yes — the tagging UI supports retroactive mapping: apply tags to route IDs and the attribution engine will recompute cost allocation for the selected window. It writes to a new export so you have an auditable revision.

[00:10:50] Priya: One more security Q — do you support FIPS endpoints for TLS and crypto ops?
[00:10:56] Nadia: We do for Private and Dedicated deployments. Hosted FIPS endpoints are available in select regions via enterprise arrangement.

[00:11:14] [00:11:14] Sofia: Wrapping up the demo portion — any other blockers we should be aware of for starting a pilot?
[00:11:20] Maya: Bandwidth for SSO+networking is our main ops work, and Priya wants to review audit and KMS docs. we'd also like to see the benchmark numbers before committing to Dedicated.
[00:11:31] Sofia: Great — so next steps: we'll send the pricing/contract template, Rahul will run the bench on your sample data, and we'll schedule a pilot kickoff next week.

[00:11:45] Liam: One last ask — can you include an example of the CSV export formatted for our ledger so we know which columns to map?
[00:11:52] Rahul: Yes, I'll attach a sample export.

[00:12:05] Sofia: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with an email that recaps action items.

[00:12:15] (cross talk and goodbyes)

[00:12:30] Post-call notes (transcriber): Occasionally mis-heard product names and acronyms; Redwood spelled correctly in most places but some speakers said 'Red Wood' in the transcript; 'KV cache' occasionally transcribed as 'K V cash' or 'K V cache'.

End of transcript.
